notes:
Second and final daf of the Phase 3 evidence-backed correction queue. Diagnosis before editing: the drift classifier reported FABRICATION-SUSPECT with 1 anchor found, 2 missing, at offset -4, and the packet carried the explicit WARNING that stub repair and link edits are forbidden here, naming rashi-reconstruction as the required remedy. That is the manifest this pass carries.

The defect was scaffold-narrated fabrication rather than compression. Every one of the 41 prior entries opened with meta-narration ('Rashi: ...', 'Rashi on ...') and then supplied essay-style commentary about the sugya at large instead of translating its own raw print line, and the links were unrelated to the segments the lines actually explain: entries 3 through 9 all pointed at l02 (the Eli's-sons verse from Samuel) while discussing Isaiah, Micah, and the three-decrees material that belongs to l12, l13, and l27. Several later entries invented content outright, including a Genesis 9:27 reading of 'yaft Elokim l'Yefet' attached to line 40, which has no counterpart anywhere in this daf's raw Rashi.

Rebuilt all 41 entries so each translates only its own raw print line, re-extracting the raw Hebrew fresh from the packet and mapping every line to its segment before writing any English. Content covers: why delaying the women's bird-offerings is reckoned as if Eli's sons had lain with them, since the women were detained from returning to their husbands and so kept from procreation (l01, lines 1-2); the notarikon reading of 'mehishtarea' as 'from ruling, one companion', the two companions being God and the image Manasseh set up in the Sanctuary, and 'tzarah' as a term of rivalry supported by the Samuel and Leviticus verses (l12, l13, lines 2-4); the Micah verse whose continuation is 'yet they lean upon the Lord', the three decrees of field, ruins, and forest heights, and the gloss of 'iyin' as ruin with its Isaiah citations (l27, lines 4-9); the revealed-sin/revealed-end contrast with the Jeremiah 29 seventy-years verse, and the Second Temple generation who were wicked in secret (l35, lines 9-14); 'the Temple will prove it' and 'set your eyes on the Temple' as the witness that the building returned to the former generations and not the latter (l36, l39, lines 14-16); Reish Lakish's rebuke of the Babylonians who did not go up in Ezra's day and so prevented the Divine Presence from resting again, with the silver-that-does-not-rot and the two-leaved-gate images for a return made only in halves (l40, lines 17-26); the cedar and sasmagor worm that hollows it from within, and Rabbi Abba's identification of the bat kol as the small remnant left (l43, lines 26-33); and Rav Pappa's resolution casting a man between them, with the four-way permutation of who was bathing and who extended the hand, closing with Reish Lakish reporting to Rabbi Yochanan (l47, lines 34-40).

Six raw lines are genuine dibbur-boundary straddles where one comment closes and the next opens inside the same print line (lines 2, 3, 4, 9, 14, 26). audit_rashi_association.py --range-from 9b --range-to 9b reports declared_associations=47 = 35*1 + 6*2, matching the hand prediction exactly, with 0 broken and 0 cross-daf.

Eight of the daf's nineteen local segments legitimately receive no Rashi comment: l02, l10, l15, l22, l24, l32, l34, and l45. These are the long scriptural quotations the Gemara itself glosses inline (most clearly l15, where the Gemara supplies its own phrase-by-phrase reading of the daughters-of-Zion verse) plus the framing questions whose wording needs no gloss. This was confirmed by tracing all 41 raw lines end to end rather than inferred from the count.

No split-citation adjustment was needed here, unlike 7a: the Isaiah 14 and ibid. 28 citations each straddle a Hebrew print break, so both were rendered whole on the line the anchor scanner attributes them to (lines 7 and 8 respectively), which is both gate-correct and the more faithful English since the break is a print-column artifact.

Post-edit evidence, re-run on the final tree: classification ALIGNED (was FABRICATION-SUSPECT), lineLevelSafe true, 3 anchors found (was 1), 0 missing (was 2), offsets [0, 0, 0], maxAbsOffset 0 - the multi-anchor-safe tier, so no attestation block is required. audit_rashi_scaffold.py 9b --no-baseline: 0 hits, which also retires the pervasive 'Rashi:' narration the prior content carried. No scaffold-baseline, repetition-baseline, or content-allowlist entry existed for 9b before or after. Entry count and vilnaLine sequence are unchanged at 41, matching the talmuddev raw lines exactly; no structural or count change was made or needed.

worker:verify --fast and --full both passed on this head, full mode including build, deploy-html, unit+render, and the browser suite. Scope is the 7 files verify reports (VERSION, target learning.json, learning_data.js, docs/rashi-audit-backlog.md, package.json/package-lock.json, plus the manifest); this self-review file is the 8th. Nothing outside the manifest was touched: 4b L61, 61a L46-64, the boundary authorization registry, 24b source he, renderer-default behavior, workflows, and hosting configuration were all left alone.
